vs_worktrunk_0_79_0_requalify.note: worktrunk's duration includes gitleaks positive/negative scans and version invocations absent from this native-git-only plan, so this is not an apples-to-apples timing comparison; recorded for reference only.

behavioral_differences_found: native `git worktree remove` refuses removal when a TRACKED file is modified, but (unverified further here) untracked-only files alone are documented upstream not to block plain removal without --force in the same way worktrunk refuses on either tracked or untracked changes; this run only exercised the modified-tracked-file case.

native `git worktree remove` does NOT delete the associated branch; worktrunk's `wt remove` deletes both worktree and branch in one step. This run needed an explicit follow-up `git branch -d` per removed worktree to reach the same end state that worktrunk reaches natively -- a real feature-parity gap for git worktree as a challenger.
native git worktree has no project-hook mechanism at all (worktrunk supports pre-start/pre-remove hooks, exercised separately in gap 9's receipt).

vs_difftastic_larger_fixture.finding: git diff --no-index succeeded (non-empty, exit 1) on all 20 files including the 2 large JSON catalogs, both Markdown docs and the large HTML file that difftastic fell back to plain-text diffing for -- but git diff's output is ALWAYS line-based/textual, never syntax-aware, so 'succeeded uniformly' is a coverage/robustness result, not a review-quality result. Difftastic's advantage (syntax-aware hunks) only applies on the 15/20 files where it parsed structurally; on those 15 it is a strictly richer diff than git diff's line-based output for the same change, though this check does not score that richness (see gap 10).

verdict_impact.explanation: This establishes the matched winner-vs-challenger comparisons gap 6 asked for on both axes (worktree isolation, structural diff) and both challengers ran successfully end to end, so gap 6's specific complaint ('no matched comparison ... exists for this layer') is addressed. Neither comparison flips the layer's keep_but_compare selection: worktrunk remains ahead on hooks and one-step branch cleanup (a genuine, newly-documented advantage over native git worktree), while difftastic's advantage over git diff is confined to the 15/20 files it parses structurally and this check does not score review quality (gap 10 does). Direction is 'inconclusive' at the overall-verdict level because the comparison surfaced real, mixed findings rather than a clean win for either incumbent or challenger.

limitations: Worktree challenger plan is a synthetic single-repo fixture, not a fork of worktrunk's exact run.py fixture; it mirrors the same steps and pass criteria but is a separate script, so timing is not directly comparable (recorded as such above).

Dirty-removal refusal was only exercised for a modified TRACKED file; the untracked-only-file refusal behavior of native git worktree was not separately tested here (worktrunk's dirty_refusal check covers both in worktrunk-0-79-0-requalify.json).

git diff --no-index challenger measures mechanical success/coverage only (exit code, non-empty output); it does not score diff quality, correctness or reviewer usefulness -- that is addressed by gap 10's blind-judge receipt in this same wave.
Both challenger runs are single-trial, synthetic or reused fixtures; no concurrency, remote, or submodule scenarios were exercised.
